P01.title: Close internet entry to the domain controller through the Ivanti Connect Secure VPN (vpn-gw-01)
P01.summary: Validation confirmed a path from the internet to the domain controller. The agent used CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887 on the corporate Ivanti Connect Secure VPN (vpn-gw-01) to get a shell on the appliance. Admin credentials cached on vpn-gw-01 also worked on the IT admin jump host (jump-it-01), and that host's admin group has RDP rights on the domain controller (dc-01), where the agent opened a read-only session. Fixing vpn-gw-01 breaks the path at its first step.
P01.why_it_matters: Anyone on the internet could take over the corporate VPN, reuse its stored admin credentials on the IT jump host, and log on to the domain controller. Control of the domain controller would let an attacker take over every account and server in the corporate domain and stage ransomware across the utility's business systems. Both flaws are among the most heavily exploited in the world and are known to be used in ransomware campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, block the Ivanti Connect Secure admin and web management interfaces on vpn-gw-01 from the internet and limit them to the internal management network; if the mitigation cannot be applied today, take vpn-gw-01 off the internet, since CISA's required action is to discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable.
Apply the fixed release and the mitigation and integrity-check steps in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887 to vpn-gw-01.

Check vpn-gw-01 for signs of compromise, including unknown files, unexpected admin accounts and configuration changes; if any are found, rebuild the appliance from a clean image and treat it as an incident.

End all active VPN and admin sessions on vpn-gw-01, then reset every admin credential cached on the appliance, working with the Windows Server team to reset the same credentials that also work on jump-it-01.
verify_steps: Confirm from an outside network that the Ivanti Connect Secure management interfaces on vpn-gw-01 are not reachable from the internet.
Confirm vpn-gw-01 runs the fixed release from the vendor's advisory and passes the vendor's integrity check.
Confirm the old admin credentials from vpn-gw-01 no longer log on to jump-it-01, then ask the validation team to rerun path P01.
P01.exec_line: Our corporate VPN can be hacked from the internet to reach the server controlling every company account; Network Engineering is fixing it now.
P01.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, the domain controller, which is marked as a crown jewel.

P02.title: Patch or restrict the field office SSL-VPN on vpn-gw-02 to break the path to domain controller dc-01
P02.summary: Validated path P02 starts at the internet-facing Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN on vpn-gw-02 (CVE-2024-21762), which gave an attacker a foothold. From there the print spooler flaw on file server fs-02 (CVE-2021-34527) gave SYSTEM access. On fs-02 a cached domain admin logon was present and was used to reach domain controller dc-01. Fixing vpn-gw-02, the entry point, breaks the whole path.
P02.why_it_matters: An outside attacker with no credentials could go from the field office VPN to full domain admin control of dc-01, which runs identity for the corporate network. That would let them sign in anywhere in the corporate environment, push ransomware widely, and disrupt the business systems the utility depends on. Both flaws on this path are widely exploited, including by ransomware groups.
fix_steps: Today, limit exposure of the Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN on vpn-gw-02: block its web and management interfaces from the internet or allow only known field office addresses, and disable SSL-VPN if field offices can work without it for now.

Upgrade FortiOS on vpn-gw-02 to the fixed release and apply the mitigation and integrity-check steps in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2024-21762. If no fix or mitigation is available, discontinue use of the SSL-VPN on vpn-gw-02 until one is.
Check vpn-gw-02 for signs of compromise: review its configuration for unknown accounts, settings or files, and review VPN logs for unusual logins since the flaw was disclosed.
End all active VPN sessions on vpn-gw-02 and reset its local admin and VPN service credentials. Ask Identity to reset the domain admin account whose logon was cached on fs-02.
verify_steps: Confirm vpn-gw-02 reports the fixed FortiOS release from the vendor's advisory and that its SSL-VPN and management interfaces are not reachable from untrusted internet addresses.
Confirm no unknown admin accounts or sessions exist on vpn-gw-02 after the session reset.
Ask the security team to rerun validation of attack path P02 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P02.exec_line: An internet-facing field office VPN flaw lets outsiders reach full control of our network directory; we are patching and restricting it now.
P02.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, the domain controller, which is marked as a crown jewel asset.

P03.title: Close contractor gateway session-token leak (nsg-01) that opens a path to the email server
P03.summary: Validated path P03 starts at the Citrix NetScaler Gateway contractor gateway (nsg-01), which is internet-facing and affected by CVE-2023-4966. Session tokens leaked by nsg-01 let a contractor session be taken over, and from that session the Microsoft Exchange Server email server (exch-01) responded to a server-side request forgery check for CVE-2022-41040. Fixing nsg-01, the entry point, breaks the whole path. exch-01 should still be patched separately by Messaging.
P03.why_it_matters: An attacker on the internet could take over a contractor's remote access session without needing a password and then reach the corporate email server. From there they could read or abuse company email, which is a common foothold for ransomware and for fraud against staff, contractors and customers. Both flaws are heavily exploited in the wild.
fix_steps: Today, limit access to the Citrix NetScaler Gateway on nsg-01 to known contractor source addresses where possible, and block its management interface from the internet.
Upgrade nsg-01 to the fixed NetScaler release and apply the mitigation and integrity-check steps in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2023-4966.
Immediately after the upgrade, end all active and persistent sessions on nsg-01 so any stolen session tokens stop working.

Check nsg-01 and the contractor accounts that used it for signs of compromise, such as sessions from unexpected locations or reused session IDs, and reset passwords for contractor accounts with suspicious activity.
Notify the Messaging team so they patch exch-01 and review it for compromise as a separate task.
verify_steps: Confirm nsg-01 reports the fixed NetScaler release from the vendor's advisory and that its management interface is not reachable from the internet.
Confirm that sessions established before the upgrade no longer work and that new contractor logins require fresh authentication.
Ask the validation team to rerun attack path P03 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P03.exec_line: A flaw in our contractor remote access gateway lets outsiders hijack sessions and reach company email; Network Engineering is patching it now.
P03.route_reason: The path ends at exch-01, the email server, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so the ticket goes directly to Network Engineering, the owner of nsg-01.

P04.title: Patch internet-facing GlobalProtect on fw-edge-03 (CVE-2024-3400) and end password reuse with OT jump host
P04.summary: Validated path P04 starts at fw-edge-03, the plant edge firewall running Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS with GlobalProtect exposed to the internet. Command injection on the GlobalProtect portal (CVE-2024-3400) was confirmed. The firewall's management account password is the same as the local admin password on ot-jump-01, the IT to OT jump host, and hist-01, the plant data historian, accepts logons from that jump host. The agent stopped at the OT boundary and did not log on to ot-jump-01 or hist-01. Fixing fw-edge-03 removes the entry point for the whole path.
P04.why_it_matters: An outside attacker could take full control of the plant edge firewall without any login, then reuse its management password to get onto the IT to OT jump host and from there into the plant data historian. That would put an attacker inside the OT DMZ with access to operational plant data and a foothold toward control systems. This flaw is among the most heavily exploited on the internet and has been used in ransomware campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, on fw-edge-03 (Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS), make sure the firewall management interface cannot be reached from the internet, and enable the Palo Alto Networks Threat Prevention protection for CVE-2024-3400 on the GlobalProtect interface until the upgrade is done.
Upgrade PAN-OS on fw-edge-03 to the fixed release listed in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2024-3400, and follow that advisory's mitigation and integrity-check steps.

After the upgrade, check fw-edge-03 for signs of compromise: review logs and configuration for unexpected changes, new accounts or unfamiliar files since the device was exposed, and escalate to incident response if anything is found.
Reset the fw-edge-03 management account password to a new unique value and end any active management sessions.

Coordinate with OT Engineering to change the local admin password on ot-jump-01 so it no longer matches any firewall credential, and to review whether hist-01 should keep accepting logons from ot-jump-01.
verify_steps: Confirm fw-edge-03 reports the fixed PAN-OS release from the vendor's advisory for CVE-2024-3400 and that the management interface is not reachable from the internet.
Confirm the fw-edge-03 management password and the ot-jump-01 local admin password are different and that the old shared password no longer works on either asset.
Rerun the autonomous validation of path P04 and confirm it no longer succeeds at fw-edge-03.
P04.exec_line: An internet-facing plant firewall flaw plus a reused password could let attackers reach our plant data historian; patching and password changes underway.
P04.route_reason: The path ends at hist-01, the plant data historian, which is marked as a crown jewel, and passes through ot-jump-01, also a crown jewel.

P05.title: Patch SQL injection in internet-facing MOVEit Transfer vendor file exchange (mft-01)
P05.summary: The validation tool confirmed a SQL injection flaw (CVE-2023-34362) in the Progress MOVEit Transfer web application on mft-01, the internet-facing vendor file exchange. An unauthenticated attacker on the internet can reach the application database. The test only read the version table, but the same flaw can expose, change or delete database contents. Fixing mft-01 closes this single-step path.
P05.why_it_matters: An outside attacker with no login could read and tamper with the database behind the vendor file exchange, exposing files and account data shared between the utility and its vendors. That could mean leaked contracts, engineering documents or customer data, breach notification duties, and a foothold for ransomware. This flaw has been used in widespread ransomware data-theft campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, restrict internet access to the Progress MOVEit Transfer web interface on mft-01 to known vendor and staff addresses, or take it offline until patched.
Upgrade MOVEit Transfer on mft-01 to the fixed release and complete the mitigation and integrity-check steps in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2023-34362.

Check mft-01 for signs of compromise: unexpected files in the web application folders, unknown or newly created user accounts, unusual database changes, and large or unexplained file downloads in the transfer logs.
Reset passwords and keys for MOVEit administrator accounts, service accounts and the database account used by mft-01, and end all active user sessions.
If any compromise is found, escalate to incident response and identify which vendor files may have been exposed.
verify_steps: Confirm the MOVEit Transfer version on mft-01 matches the fixed release named in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2023-34362.
Confirm from an outside network that the web interface is reachable only from approved addresses, as intended.
Ask the security team to rerun validation of attack path P05 against mft-01 and confirm the SQL injection no longer succeeds.
P05.exec_line: Our internet-facing vendor file exchange has a widely abused flaw letting outsiders reach its data; we are patching and locking it down now.
P05.route_reason: The path ends at mft-01, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it can go directly to Enterprise Applications.

P06.title: Close internet-reachable admin setup on Partner wiki (wiki-ext, Confluence CVE-2023-22515)
P06.summary: Validation confirmed that the setup endpoint on the Partner wiki (wiki-ext), an internet-facing Atlassian Confluence Data Center instance, is reachable from the internet and would let an outsider create a Confluence administrator account. The agent stopped before creating an account. Fixing wiki-ext closes this single-step path.
P06.why_it_matters: An outsider could make themselves an administrator of the Partner wiki and read, change or delete everything shared with partners there, including documents that may describe utility projects and contacts. Admin control of the wiki could also be used to plant malicious content for partners and staff or as a foothold for ransomware, and this flaw is widely exploited.
fix_steps: Today, block internet access to the Partner wiki (wiki-ext) Confluence Data Center setup and administration pages, or take wiki-ext off the internet until it is patched.
Upgrade Atlassian Confluence Data Center on wiki-ext to the fixed release and apply the mitigation and integrity-check steps in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2023-22515.
Check wiki-ext for evidence of compromise: review the administrator group for accounts that were not created by your team, and look for unexpected new users, plugins or configuration changes.

If anything suspicious is found, remove the unauthorized accounts, end all active sessions, reset Confluence administrator credentials on wiki-ext, and report the findings to Security so they can be reported to CISA.
verify_steps: From an external network, confirm the Confluence setup and administration pages on wiki-ext are not reachable.
Confirm in the Confluence administration console that wiki-ext runs the fixed release and that the administrator group contains only approved accounts.
Ask the security team to rerun validation of attack path P06 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P06.exec_line: Our partner wiki could let an outsider make themselves administrator from the internet; we are blocking access and patching it now.
P06.route_reason: The path ends at wiki-ext, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it can go straight to the Collaboration Tools team.

P07.title: Close internet-exposed ScreenConnect console rmm-01 that opens a path to the virtualization cluster esxi-07
P07.summary: Validated path P07 starts at rmm-01, the internet-facing ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote support console, where the setup wizard was reachable without authentication (CVE-2024-1709). An attacker could create an administrator account there. Because the hypervisor hosts on esxi-07 (VMware ESXi) trust a directory group that the support console can create, that foothold could be used to gain full control of the virtualization cluster (CVE-2024-37085). Fixing rmm-01 breaks the path at its entry point.
P07.why_it_matters: An outsider could take over the remote support console and from there gain full control of the virtualization cluster that runs many corporate servers. That would let them shut down, encrypt or tamper with business systems across the utility at once, which is a common ransomware pattern. Both flaws are known to be used in ransomware attacks.
fix_steps: Today, remove internet access to the ConnectWise ScreenConnect management interface on rmm-01, allowing it only from approved internal or VPN addresses.

Upgrade ConnectWise ScreenConnect on rmm-01 to the fixed release and apply the mitigation and integrity-check steps in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2024-1709; if no fix can be applied, take rmm-01 out of service.
Check rmm-01 for compromise: review all administrator and user accounts on the console, remove any you did not create, and review the console's activity history for unknown sessions or changes.
End all active sessions on rmm-01 and reset the console administrator passwords and any directory credentials the console uses.
Tell Infrastructure (owner of esxi-07) about any accounts or directory groups the console created so they can confirm the hypervisor's trusted admin group has not been re-created or altered.
verify_steps: From an outside network, confirm the ScreenConnect management interface and setup wizard on rmm-01 cannot be reached.
Confirm rmm-01 runs the fixed release named in the vendor advisory and that the account list contains only approved administrators.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of attack path P07 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P07.exec_line: Our internet-facing remote support tool could let attackers seize the server virtualization cluster; we are locking it down and patching now.
P07.route_reason: The path ends at esxi-07, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes straight to the IT Service Desk as owner of rmm-01.

P08.title: P08: Close internet-exposed Cisco IOS XE Web UI on substation router rtr-sub-12 (path to EMS data link)
P08.summary: The Cisco IOS XE Web UI on the substation comms router rtr-sub-12 is reachable from the internet and runs an affected version (CVE-2023-20198). From that router, a route reaches the energy management system data link ems-link-01 with no access list in between. Validation confirmed both conditions but sent no traffic to the EMS link. Fixing rtr-sub-12, the first step, breaks the path.
P08.why_it_matters: An attacker on the internet could take full control of the substation router and use it as a bridge onto the energy management system data link, a crown jewel asset. That could let them interfere with the data grid operators rely on to monitor and control the system. This flaw is among the most widely exploited on the internet.
fix_steps: Today, take the Cisco IOS XE Web UI on rtr-sub-12 off the internet: disable it or restrict it so it is reachable only from a trusted management network, as BOD 23-02 requires for management interfaces.
Upgrade rtr-sub-12 to the fixed Cisco IOS XE release and apply the mitigation and integrity-check steps in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2023-20198.
Check rtr-sub-12 for signs of compromise, especially unrecognized local accounts with privilege level 15 or unexpected configuration changes, and report any positive finding to CISA immediately.
Remove any unrecognized accounts, end active management sessions, and reset all administrative credentials on rtr-sub-12.
Work with Grid Operations to add an access list between the substation comms network and the EMS data link ems-link-01 as a second layer of defense.
verify_steps: From an external network, confirm the rtr-sub-12 Web UI does not respond.
Confirm rtr-sub-12 runs the fixed release named in the vendor's advisory and shows only approved local accounts.
Request a rerun of the validation for path P08 to confirm it no longer succeeds.
P08.exec_line: An internet-exposed substation router could give attackers a path to our energy management system link; we are closing it now.
P08.route_reason: The path ends at ems-link-01, the energy management system data link, which is marked as a crown jewel.

P09.title: Patch Apache Log4j2 on the internet-facing Outage map API (outage-api)
P09.summary: Validation confirmed that the Outage map API (outage-api), an internet-facing Java service that uses Apache Log4j2, is exploitable through CVE-2021-44228. A harmless lookup string sent in a request header caused the service to make an outbound DNS query, which shows that attacker-controlled input is processed by the vulnerable logging library. This is the only step on the path, so fixing outage-api closes it.
P09.why_it_matters: An attacker on the internet could run their own code on the server behind the public outage map and use it as a foothold inside the utility's network. That could take down or falsify outage information that customers rely on during storms and emergencies, and could be the first step toward ransomware. This flaw is among the most widely exploited and has known ransomware use.
fix_steps: Today, block outbound connections from the Outage map API (outage-api) servers to the internet except the specific destinations the service needs, and put the API behind a web application firewall rule that drops requests containing lookup strings in headers or parameters.

Upgrade Apache Log4j2 in the outage-api Java service to a fixed release, using the vendor's advisory for CVE-2021-44228 for the fixed version and its mitigation and integrity-check steps. If it cannot be upgraded promptly, take outage-api off the internet until it is, since temporary mitigations are acceptable only until an update is applied.
Rebuild and redeploy the outage-api application so no copy of the vulnerable Log4j2 library remains in its packages, containers or dependent libraries.

After the upgrade, check outage-api for signs of compromise: review web, application and DNS logs since the service went live for lookup strings and unexpected outbound connections, and look for unknown processes, files or scheduled tasks on the host.
If any sign of compromise is found, isolate the host, rebuild it from a known-good image, and reset all credentials, API keys and secrets stored on or used by outage-api.
verify_steps: Confirm the software inventory or dependency scan of the deployed outage-api build shows only the fixed Apache Log4j2 release and no older copies.
Confirm outage-api servers cannot make outbound connections to arbitrary internet hosts and that the firewall rule blocking lookup strings is active.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of attack path P09 against outage-api and confirm no outbound DNS query is triggered.
P09.exec_line: Our public outage map service has a widely exploited flaw that could let outsiders take control; the applications team is patching it now.
P09.route_reason: The path ends at outage-api, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes directly to the owner team, Customer Applications.

P10.title: Close unauthenticated access to the Fortinet FortiManager device registration port on fmgr-01
P10.summary: Validation confirmed that the device registration port on the Firewall manager (fmgr-01, Fortinet FortiManager, corporate zone) answers from the corporate user network and runs a version affected by CVE-2024-47575. This flaw lets a remote attacker run code on the manager without logging in. The path is a single step, so fixing fmgr-01 closes it.
P10.why_it_matters: An attacker on the corporate user network could take full control of the system that manages the utility's firewalls without any credentials. From there they could read or change firewall rules and configurations across the network, weakening the boundaries that protect operational systems. This flaw is already widely exploited in real attacks.
fix_steps: Today, restrict the device registration port on the Firewall manager (fmgr-01, Fortinet FortiManager) so that only the managed firewalls can reach it, and block it from the corporate user network and the internet.
Upgrade FortiManager on fmgr-01 to the fixed release and apply the mitigation and integrity-check steps in the vendor's advisory for CVE-2024-47575.

Check fmgr-01 for signs of compromise: review the list of registered devices for any unknown or unexpected entries, and review recent changes to managed firewall configurations and administrator accounts.

If anything suspicious is found, treat fmgr-01 as compromised, rebuild it from a trusted state, and reset the FortiManager administrator credentials and any credentials it stores for the managed firewalls.
verify_steps: From a host on the corporate user network, confirm the device registration port on fmgr-01 no longer answers, while managed firewalls still connect normally.
Confirm in the FortiManager system information on fmgr-01 that it runs the fixed release named in the vendor's advisory.
Request a rerun of the validation for path P10 to confirm the path is closed.
P10.exec_line: Attackers on our office network could seize the system that controls our firewalls; we are locking it down and patching it.
P10.route_reason: The path ends at fmgr-01, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes straight to Network Engineering.

P11.title: Patch Netlogon (Zerologon) flaw on domain controller dc-01
P11.summary: The validation agent confirmed that domain controller dc-01 (Microsoft Windows Server, Active Directory) runs a version affected by CVE-2020-1472 (Zerologon). It also confirmed that dc-01 accepts Netlogon secure channels from corporate workstations. The agent checked the version only and made no change. Fixing dc-01 closes this single-step path.
P11.why_it_matters: Anyone with a foothold on a corporate workstation could take control of dc-01 and, through it, every account and computer in the Active Directory domain. That would give an attacker the keys to deploy ransomware or reach systems that support utility operations. This flaw is among the most widely exploited and is known to be used in ransomware campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, limit which networks can reach Netlogon and RPC on dc-01 to domain-joined systems and management hosts that need it, and increase monitoring of authentication activity on dc-01 until it is patched.

Apply the Microsoft Windows Server update that fixes CVE-2020-1472 to dc-01 and to every other domain controller in the domain. Use the vendor's advisory for CVE-2020-1472 for the fixed release and its mitigation and enforcement steps.

After patching, check dc-01 for signs of compromise: unexpected changes to the domain controller computer account, new or changed privileged accounts and group memberships, and unusual Netlogon activity in the security logs.
If any sign of compromise is found, treat the domain as compromised. Escalate to incident response and reset the domain controller computer account credentials and privileged domain credentials.
verify_steps: Confirm that dc-01 and all other domain controllers report the update for CVE-2020-1472 as installed.

Confirm that Netlogon connections to dc-01 are reachable only from the allowed systems, and that the domain controller event logs show no rejected or vulnerable secure channel attempts that remain unexplained.
Rerun the validation of attack path P11 against dc-01 and confirm it is no longer exploitable.
P11.exec_line: Our main domain controller has a widely exploited flaw that could let an attacker take over all company accounts; patching now.
P11.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, which is marked as a crown jewel asset.

P12.title: Restrict RDP and require MFA on OT jump host ot-jump-01 to cut the corporate path to EMS data link ems-link-01
P12.summary: Validation path P12 confirmed that the IT to OT jump host (ot-jump-01, Microsoft Windows Server, OT DMZ) shows an RDP logon prompt to a corporate desktop VLAN and accepts password-only sign-in. The Energy management system data link (ems-link-01) trusts logons coming from ot-jump-01, so anyone who signs in to the jump host could reach the EMS data link. The validation agent reached the logon prompt but did not attempt a logon. No CVEs are involved. These are configuration issues, and fixing the entry point on ot-jump-01 breaks the path.
P12.why_it_matters: An attacker on any corporate desktop, for example after a phishing compromise, could guess or reuse a password to sign in to the OT jump host and then be trusted by the energy management system data link. That link feeds the system grid operators use to monitor and control the power system, so misuse could disrupt or falsify grid operations data. It would also likely be a compliance finding for remote access controls on OT systems.
fix_steps: On the IT to OT jump host ot-jump-01 (Microsoft Windows Server), restrict inbound RDP at the firewall today so only a named group of approved administrator workstations or a dedicated remote access subnet can reach it, not the whole corporate network.
Require multi-factor authentication for every RDP sign-in to ot-jump-01 and disable password-only remote logon.
Limit which accounts may sign in over RDP to ot-jump-01 to a small, named OT Engineering group and remove any unused or shared accounts.
Review ot-jump-01 sign-in logs for unexpected RDP logons from corporate desktop subnets, and reset passwords for any accounts with suspicious activity.
Coordinate with Grid Operations to confirm which ot-jump-01 accounts ems-link-01 trusts and narrow that trust to only the accounts that need it.
verify_steps: From a corporate desktop VLAN outside the approved group, confirm the RDP service on ot-jump-01 is unreachable.
From an approved administrator workstation, confirm an RDP sign-in to ot-jump-01 prompts for multi-factor authentication and fails without it.
Request a rerun of the validation for path P12 to confirm the path from the corporate network to ems-link-01 is closed.
P12.exec_line: Any corporate computer could reach the gateway into our grid control systems with only a password; we are locking it down.
P12.route_reason: The path ends at ems-link-01, the energy management system data link, which is marked as a crown jewel. The fix point ot-jump-01 is also a crown jewel.
